title: Kernel admission matrix and signal negotiation manual
author: Jordan Kim
content:
Summary:
This document defines the kernel admission matrix and the signal negotiation protocol used between the runtime request router, the scheduler, and kernel instances. It provides a prescriptive matrix of signals and thresholds, sample policy YAML for the admission broker, instrumentation guidance, an operational runbook for admission-related incidents, and a rollout checklist for changes to the admission logic.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: runtime engineers, scheduler owners, SREs, and reliability-focused product engineers.
- Scope: admission decision inputs and outputs, signal definitions, negotiation rounds, safety gates for degradation, and testing/rollout steps.

Goals:
- Make admission decisions deterministic and auditable across heterogeneous GPU pools.
- Preserve latency SLOs by prioritizing low-latency cohorts while allowing controlled degradation for best-effort traffic.
- Provide a safe negotiation protocol that avoids oscillation when kernel availability fluctuates.

Key concepts:
1) Admission broker: a small, deterministic service colocated with the request router responsible for converting traffic intent into kernel "slot" requests.
2) Signals: typed metrics used in negotiation (see table below).
3) Negotiation round: a single exchange in which the broker proposes a slot profile and kernel replies with an acceptance, partial-accept, or reject.
4) Slot profile: an immutable descriptor (model variant, max_seq_len, prioritization_token, quality_tier) used to match kernel capabilities.

Signals and metrics (definitions):
- runtime.admit.latency_ms: time taken by the admission broker to respond to router before handoff.
- kernel.acceptance_rate: fraction of proposals accepted by kernels per 1m window.
- scheduler.queue_depth: number of pending kernel requests.
- kernel.available_slots: sum of free execution slots across matched kernels.
- fidelity.headroom_pct: estimated percentage of quality headroom remaining if requested batch is admitted.
- kvcache.warmth_score: heuristic (0.0-1.0) of prefix cache locality expected for the request.

Admission decision matrix (human-readable table):
| Traffic class | Min SLO p50 (ms) | Max allowed queue_depth | Min kernel.available_slots | kvcache.warmth_score min | Default action |
|---------------|------------------:|------------------------:|--------------------------:|------------------------:|----------------|
| interactive (high) | 50 | 10 | 4 | 0.6 | accept-or-hedge
| standard | 150 | 40 | 2 | 0.4 | accept-if-available-else-queue
| background | 500 | 200 | 0 | 0.0 | best-effort / defer or quantized variant

Interpretation notes:
- queue_depth and available_slots are averaged with an EWMA alpha=0.33 over 10s.
- fidelity.headroom_pct is estimated from the latest quality model and is used to decide whether a cheaper quantized kernel can be used.

Policy example (admission-broker.yaml):
```yaml
version: v1
policies:
  - name: interactive-strict
    traffic_class: interactive
    max_queue_depth: 10
    min_available_slots: 4
    allowed_variants: [gpu-full, gpu-quantized-8bit]
    fallback_sequence: [gpu-full, gpu-quantized-8bit, cpu-approx]
    gating:
      - metric: fidelity.headroom_pct
        operator: ">="
        value: 0.25
      - metric: kvcache.warmth_score
        operator: ">="
        value: 0.6
  - name: background-queueable
    traffic_class: background
    max_queue_depth: 200
    min_available_slots: 0
    allowed_variants: [gpu-quantized-8bit, cpu-approx]
    fallback_sequence: [gpu-quantized-8bit, cpu-approx]
```

Negotiation protocol (sequence):
1) Router -> Broker: send request envelope with traffic_class, model_id, seq_len, prompt_hash, provenance.
2) Broker -> Candidate kernels: issue propose(slot_profile) with TTL=250ms for interactive and 1s for background.
3) Kernel -> Broker: respond accept | partial-accept(capacity=N) | reject(reason). Include kernel.acceptance_rate in response header.
4) Broker: pick best fit; if partial-accept, issue hedged-proposals to fallback kernels.
5) Router: on accept, proxy request to kernel with a short-circuit shadow to fallback path for observability.

Safety gates and anti-oscillation rules:
- Hysteresis windows: any admission change that increases allowed queue_depth or relaxes fidelity must be held for 30s before acceptance.
- Rate-limit admission changes to 1 update per 10s per shard.
- If kernel.acceptance_rate < 0.2 for 60s, automatically trigger fallback to lower-fidelity variants and alert SRE.

Instrumentation and telemetry contract (required metrics):
- runtime.admission.e2e_time_ms (p50/p95/p99)
- runtime.admission.rejections.count (by reason)
- kernel.accept_response_latency_ms
- kernel.acceptance_rate (1m, 5m rollups)
- scheduler.queue_depth (per shard)
- kernel.available_slots (per variant)
- admission.negotiation_rounds.count
- fidelity.degradation_events.count

Recommended dashboards and alerts:
- Dashboard: "Admission health" showing p95 admit latency, acceptance_rate heatmap, queue_depth by traffic class, and trending of fidelity_degradations.
- Alerts:
  - P0: p95 runtime.admission.e2e_time_ms > 400ms for >3m or kernel.acceptance_rate < 0.15 for 2m.
  - P1: sudden increase (>3x) in admission.rejections.count within 5m.

Operational runbook: admission failures
1) Symptom: spikes in "admission.e2e_time_ms" or mass rejections for interactive traffic.
2) Immediate checks (run these in order):
   a) Check broker process health: curl http://broker.local/healthz (expect 200).
   b) Query metrics: `kubectl get --namespace=runtime -l app=admission-broker -o jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.name}'` then `kubectl port-forward svc/admission-broker 8080:8080` and `curl localhost:8080/metrics | grep admission`.
   c) Inspect kernel pool: `rctl kernel list --variant=gpu-full --shard=<shard>` and verify kernel.available_slots > policy.min_available_slots.
   d) Check scheduler queue depth: `promql "sum(scheduler_queue_depth) by (shard)"` in Grafana Explore.
3) Remediation steps (ordered):
   1) If broker CPU is saturated: scale broker replicas by +2 and pin to dedicated node pool.
   2) If kernel.acceptance_rate is low: mark problematic kernel nodes unschedulable and drain for further investigation: `rctl kernel drain <kernel-id> --reason=acceptance-drop`
   3) If queue_depth is high: temporarily shift background traffic to rate-limited route: `rctl route update background --throttle=0.2`
   4) If fidelity.headroom_pct low for interactive: enable forced fallback variant for interactive for 5 minutes: `rctl policy set interactive-strict --force-variant=gpu-quantized-8bit --ttl=300s`
4) Post-incident: run the admission regression harness (see Testing section) and file an incident with tags: `admission, kernel, degradation`

Testing and rollout checklist:
- Unit tests for policy parser with synthetic signals.
- Integration test: simulate 3 negotiation rounds with mixed kernel responses; assert router receives accept within TTL 99% of the time in synthetic load.
- Shadow rollout: enable new negotiation logic in 10% of routers for 48h and compare fidelity.degradation_events.count and admit latency.
- Canary: 2% live traffic gating for 2h, then 10% for 4h, then 50% for 4h, monitor p95 admit latency and kernel.acceptance_rate.

Admission regression harness (how to run):
- Repo: infra/runtime-admission/tests/harness
- Command: `make run-harness ENV=staging PROFILE=interactive THREADS=200 DURATION=10m`
- Outputs: CSV of admission.latency, accept_rate, fallback_usage.

Configuration and example knobs (table):
| Field | Type | Default | Recommended change window |
|-------|------|--------:|--------------------------:|
| max_queue_depth | integer | 40 | immediate (tweak small steps) |
| min_available_slots | integer | 2 | 30s hysteresis |
| negotiation_ttl_ms | integer | 250 | testing only |
| admission_hysteresis_s | integer | 30 | config change must observe for 30s |

Troubleshooting scenar os (short):
- Symptom: oscillation between full-fidelity and quantized kernels.
  Action: increase hysteresis window to 60s, enable smoothing on fidelity.headroom_pct to 30s EWMA.
- Symptom: headroom reports high but users see poor quality.
  Action: run fidelity-sample-set against the quantized variant and verify objective metrics (BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-similarity).

Ownership and escalation:
- Primary owner: runtime-scheduler team (oncall alias: #oncall-runtime-scheduler)
- Secondary owner: kernel-team (oncall alias: #oncall-kernel)
- Pager rule: any P0 alert must page runtime-scheduler oncall immediately and create an incident in PagerDuty.

References and related artifacts:

- Link: /eng-serving-runtime/profiling-playbook/causal-latency-attribution-and-signal-enrichment-playbook-2026 (observability method)

Appendix: diagram (text):
- "Broker negotiation flow": a sequence diagram where Router -> Broker (envelope) -> Kernel candidates; kernels respond; Broker decides; Router proxies. Include correlation IDs for every exchange and attach them to tracing span `admission.negotiation.span`.
